input_signals.name: Rich Sales Multiple Issuance
input_signals.hypothesis: Equity issuance is especially bearish when the firm already trades at a high price-to-sales multiple.
input_signals.reasoning: A high sales multiple indicates optimistic market pricing relative to the firm’s revenue base. When management issues stock under that condition, the financing action may reveal that insiders view the valuation as favorable to sellers rather than buyers.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( mul( prcc_f, csho ), sale ) ), rank( ratio( sstk, at ) ) )

input_signals.name: Thresholded Equity Timing Confirmation
input_signals.hypothesis: Repurchases are most bullish when the firm trades below book value, while equity issuance is most bearish when the firm trades at a rich price-to-book multiple.
input_signals.reasoning: This avoids the prior mechanical inverse-rank spread by activating financing flows only in valuation regions where managerial timing is economically informative. Below-book buybacks suggest management is retiring underpriced equity, while issuance above two times book suggests opportunistic sale of overvalued shares.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: winsor( sub( mul( ratio( prstkc, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), indicator( ratio( ceq, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), 1 ) ), mul( ratio( sstk, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), indicator( ratio( mul( prcc_f, csho ), ceq ), 2 ) ) ), 1 )

input_signals.name: Cash-Rich Rich Issuer
input_signals.hypothesis: Expensive firms issuing equity despite already high cash balances should underperform.
input_signals.reasoning: This avoids the mechanical leverage-denominator problem by using lagged cash holdings rather than contemporaneous debt-to-assets changes. If a richly valued firm sells equity even though it entered the period cash-rich, the issuance is more plausibly opportunistic market timing than necessary financing.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: winsor( mul( indicator( ratio( mul( prcc_f, csho ), sale ), 2 ), mul( ratio( sstk, at ), lag( ratio( che, at ), 1 ) ) ), 1 )

input_signals.name: Cash-Backed Net Retirement
input_signals.hypothesis: Net equity retirement should be most bullish when the firm entered the period with high cash relative to market value.
input_signals.reasoning: High cash-to-market value indicates a balance-sheet-backed form of cheapness, where repurchases may be funded from liquid resources rather than external financing. Using net repurchases penalizes firms that report buybacks while simultaneously issuing equity, focusing on genuine shareholder accretion.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: winsor( mul( lag( ratio( che, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), 1 ), ratio( sub( prstkc, sstk ), lag( at, 1 ) ) ), 1 )

input_signals.name: Discounted Repurchase Payout Tilt
input_signals.hypothesis: High book-to-market firms should outperform when management shifts payout policy toward repurchases rather than cash dividends.
input_signals.reasoning: This removes the hard below-book gate and avoids the change-in-net-issuance construct by focusing on payout form rather than dilution reversal. For cheap firms, an incremental tilt from dividends toward repurchases is more plausibly valuation-sensitive because managers choose the flexible payout channel when they believe shares are underpriced.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: winsor( mul( rank( ratio( ceq, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), delta( ratio( sub( prstkc, dvc ), lag( at, 1 ) ), 1 ) ), 1 )

input_signals.name: Net-Cash Retirement Conviction
input_signals.hypothesis: Net equity retirement should be more bullish when the firm entered the period with a high net-cash position relative to market value.
input_signals.reasoning: This refines the cash-backed retirement idea by distinguishing liquid balance-sheet support from cash that is offset by debt. Ranking the lagged net-cash-to-market measure avoids sign-pathology from levered firms while preserving the idea that buybacks funded from excess liquidity are more credible undervaluation signals.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: winsor( mul( rank( lag( ratio( sub( che, add( dltt, dlc ) ), mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), 1 ) ), ratio( sub( prstkc, sstk ), lag( at, 1 ) ) ), 1 )

input_signals.name: Profitless Peer-Rich Issuer
input_signals.hypothesis: Equity issuance by peer-expensive firms should be most bearish when operating margins are weak.
input_signals.reasoning: High price-to-sales can be justified for firms with strong scalable margins, so conditioning on weak EBITDA margin targets overvaluation that is less fundamentally supported. The margin term is independent of the issuance proceeds and avoids the prior asset-denominator mechanical problem.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: winsor( mul( indicator( ind_zscore( ratio( mul( prcc_f, csho ), sale ) ), 0 ), mul( ratio( sstk, lag( at, 1 ) ), rank( neg( ratio( ebitda, sale ) ) ) ) ), 1 )

input_signals.name: Persistent Sales-Yield Retirement
input_signals.hypothesis: Sustained net equity retirement should be most bullish for firms that are cheap relative to their sales base.
input_signals.reasoning: A multi-year net retirement measure filters out one-off buybacks and focuses on persistent reductions in the equity base. Interacting it with sales yield captures management repeatedly retiring shares when the market price is low relative to operating scale.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: winsor( mul( ratio( sale, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), ratio( ts_sum( sub( prstkc, sstk ), 3 ), lag( at, 1 ) ) ), 1 )

input_signals.name: Peer-Weighted Gross Timing Spread
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms should outperform when gross repurchases occur at peer-cheap valuations and underperform when gross issuance occurs at peer-rich valuations.
input_signals.reasoning: This fixes the algebraic collapse by using gross repurchase and gross issuance legs rather than signed net equity flow in both branches. Continuous industry-relative valuation weights avoid an all-zero hard gate while still giving the long side to cheap repurchasers and the short side to rich issuers.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: winsor( sub( mul( ratio( prstkc, lag( at, 1 ) ), rank( neg( ind_zscore( ratio( mul( prcc_f, csho ), sale ) ) ) ) ), mul( ratio( sstk, lag( at, 1 ) ), rank( ind_zscore( ratio( mul( prcc_f, csho ), sale ) ) ) ) ), 1 )

input_signals.name: Cashflow-Surplus Peer-Rich Issuer
input_signals.hypothesis: Equity issuance by peer-expensive firms should be especially bearish when the firm already had strong operating cash flow relative to sales.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces noisy issuance acceleration with a financing-need diagnostic: firms with strong prior cash-flow margins have less fundamental need to sell equity. If such firms issue while trading rich relative to peers, the action is more likely opportunistic market timing than necessary financing.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: winsor( mul( ind_zscore( ratio( mul( prcc_f, csho ), sale ) ), mul( ratio( sstk, lag( at, 1 ) ), rank( lag( ratio( oancf, sale ), 1 ) ) ) ), 1 )

input_signals.name: Peer-Rich Equity Debt Takeout
input_signals.hypothesis: Equity issuance should be bearish when peer-expensive firms use equity capital to retire debt.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the cosmetic lagged-valuation variant with a distinct use-of-proceeds mechanism. Using the actual debt-retirement flow avoids the mechanical leverage-ratio problem, while the MIN term requires both equity issuance and debt takeout rather than merely rewarding a generic issuance level.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: winsor( mul( ind_zscore( ratio( mul( prcc_f, csho ), sale ) ), min( ratio( sstk, lag( at, 1 ) ), ratio( dltr, lag( at, 1 ) ) ) ), 1 )

input_signals.name: Peer-Rich Roundtrip Equity Flow
input_signals.hypothesis: Peer-expensive firms that both issue and repurchase equity should underperform.
input_signals.reasoning: This avoids the incoherent MIN-of-ranks dilution construction by using gross equity flows directly: the signal is high only when issuance and repurchases coexist. At rich valuations, simultaneous issuance and buybacks can indicate dilution camouflage, option-compensation recycling, or EPS management rather than genuine undervaluation-driven repurchases.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: winsor( mul( ind_zscore( ratio( mul( prcc_f, csho ), sale ) ), ratio( min( sstk, prstkc ), lag( at, 1 ) ) ), 1 )

input_signals.name: Peer-Cheap Sales-Per-Share Buyback
input_signals.hypothesis: Repurchases should be most bullish when peer-cheap firms also generate rising sales per share.
input_signals.reasoning: This shifts away from a pure share-shrinkage anomaly by requiring evidence that repurchases are associated with operating-scale accretion per share. A cheap firm buying back stock while sales per share rises is more likely creating value for remaining shareholders than simply shrinking because the business is contracting.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: winsor( mul( rank( neg( ind_zscore( ratio( mul( prcc_f, csho ), sale ) ) ) ), mul( ratio( prstkc, lag( at, 1 ) ), growth( ratio( sale, csho ), 1 ) ) ), 1 )

input_signals.name: Peer-Rich Net-Dilutive Roundtrip
input_signals.hypothesis: Gross equity roundtripping should be most bearish when peer-expensive firms are also net issuers.
input_signals.reasoning: This is not an EV/S denominator swap; it refines the strong roundtrip result by distinguishing neutral churn from roundtrip activity that still leaves shareholders diluted. At rich peer-relative valuations, simultaneous issuance and repurchases are especially suspect when issuance dominates repurchase, consistent with dilution camouflage or opportunistic equity sale.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: winsor( mul( ind_zscore( ratio( mul( prcc_f, csho ), sale ) ), mul( ratio( min( sstk, prstkc ), lag( at, 1 ) ), rank( ratio( sub( sstk, prstkc ), lag( at, 1 ) ) ) ) ), 1 )

input_signals.name: Peer-Rich Equity-Funded Payout
input_signals.hypothesis: Expensive firms issuing equity while simultaneously distributing cash to shareholders should underperform.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the cash-flow-surplus scaling variant with a use-of-proceeds mechanism: the firm raises equity while still paying out through repurchases or dividends. For peer-rich firms, that combination suggests management may be exploiting overvaluation to fund shareholder distributions rather than financing productive investment.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: winsor( mul( ind_zscore( ratio( mul( prcc_f, csho ), sale ) ), ratio( min( sstk, add( prstkc, dvc ) ), lag( at, 1 ) ) ), 1 )

input_signals.name: Peer-Cheap EBITDA-Per-Share Buyback
input_signals.hypothesis: Repurchases should be most bullish when peer-cheap firms also show improving operating earnings per share.
input_signals.reasoning: This moves away from the failed smoothed payout-tilt template and asks whether buybacks are accompanied by operating per-share accretion. A cheap firm repurchasing shares while EBITDA per share rises is more likely confirming undervaluation than merely reallocating payout form.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: winsor( mul( rank( neg( ind_zscore( ratio( mul( prcc_f, csho ), sale ) ) ) ), mul( ratio( prstkc, lag( at, 1 ) ), ratio( delta( ratio( ebitda, csho ), 1 ), prcc_f ) ) ), 1 )

input_signals.name: Peer-Rich Roundtrip Sales Fade
input_signals.hypothesis: Gross equity roundtripping should be most bearish when peer-expensive firms also show weak or declining sales growth.
input_signals.reasoning: High price-to-sales can be defensible for firms with strong revenue growth, which may dilute the signal from valuation alone. When a peer-rich firm is churning equity while sales growth fades, the financing behavior is less likely to support genuine expansion and more likely to reflect opportunistic dilution or earnings-management optics.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: winsor( mul( ind_zscore( ratio( mul( prcc_f, csho ), sale ) ), mul( ratio( min( sstk, prstkc ), lag( at, 1 ) ), rank( neg( growth( sale, 1 ) ) ) ) ), 1 )

input_signals.name: Peer-Cheap Buyback Accretion Gap
input_signals.hypothesis: Repurchases should be most bullish when peer-cheap firms improve sales per share beyond what is explained by total sales growth.
input_signals.reasoning: This fixes the sign inconsistency by using gross repurchase intensity and a ranked accretion gap rather than multiplying two potentially negative terms. The signal targets cheap firms where buybacks plausibly enhance per-share operating scale, not net issuers with deteriorating fundamentals.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: winsor( mul( rank( neg( ind_zscore( ratio( mul( prcc_f, csho ), sale ) ) ) ), mul( ratio( prstkc, lag( at, 1 ) ), rank( sub( growth( ratio( sale, csho ), 1 ), growth( sale, 1 ) ) ) ) ), 1 )

input_signals.name: Peer-Rich Equity Debt Co-Issue
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms that are expensive relative to peers and simultaneously raise both equity and long-term debt should underperform.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces another roundtrip-equity variant with a distinct capital-market-window mechanism. The MIN term is high only when both equity and debt issuance are present, identifying peer-rich firms broadly tapping external capital rather than merely appearing in a standard equity-issuance sort.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: winsor( mul( ind_zscore( ratio( mul( prcc_f, csho ), sale ) ), ratio( min( sstk, dltis ), lag( at, 1 ) ) ), 1 )

input_signals.name: Peer-Rich Noncash Dilution
input_signals.hypothesis: Share-count dilution should be especially bearish for peer-expensive firms when it is not explained by cash equity issuance proceeds.
input_signals.reasoning: This moves away from the saturated roundtrip family and focuses on noncash or low-cash dilution, such as stock compensation, acquisition shares, or option-related issuance. At rich peer-relative valuations, dilution that expands shares without comparable cash proceeds is more consistent with overvalued equity being used as currency than with productive financing.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: winsor( mul( ind_zscore( ratio( mul( prcc_f, csho ), sale ) ), rank( sub( growth( csho, 1 ), ratio( sstk, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ) ) ), 1 )

input_signals.name: Peer-Rich Short-Debt Pressure Issuer
input_signals.hypothesis: Equity issuance by peer-expensive firms should be most bearish when short-term debt is also increasing.
input_signals.reasoning: This avoids the ambiguous asset-growth residual and instead tests a financing-pressure channel. If a richly valued firm sells equity while short-term debt rises, the firm may be relying heavily on external capital despite favorable market pricing, raising overinvestment or liquidity-stress concerns.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: winsor( mul( ind_zscore( ratio( mul( prcc_f, csho ), sale ) ), mul( ratio( sstk, lag( at, 1 ) ), rank( ratio( delta( dlc, 1 ), lag( at, 1 ) ) ) ) ), 1 )

input_signals.name: Peer-Rich Buyback Reversal Issuer
input_signals.hypothesis: Expensive firms that issue equity after recently repurchasing shares should underperform.
input_signals.reasoning: This tests a financing-policy reversal rather than simultaneous roundtripping. A firm that was buying back shares but then sells equity when peer valuation is rich may be revealing that the prior repurchase was not true undervaluation conviction, or that management is now timing an overvalued equity market.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: winsor( mul( ind_zscore( ratio( mul( prcc_f, csho ), sale ) ), mul( ratio( sstk, lag( at, 1 ) ), rank( ratio( lag( prstkc, 1 ), lag( at, 1 ) ) ) ) ), 1 )

input_signals.name: Peer-Rich Cash-Drain Issuer
input_signals.hypothesis: Equity issuance by peer-expensive firms should be most bearish when cash balances still decline.
input_signals.reasoning: Unlike prior cash-parking ideas, this avoids the mechanical tendency of issuance to raise cash by looking for the opposite case: cash falls despite equity proceeds. For a richly valued issuer, that pattern suggests rapid cash consumption, hidden financing need, or low-return use of proceeds rather than value-creating investment.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: winsor( mul( ind_zscore( ratio( mul( prcc_f, csho ), sale ) ), mul( ratio( sstk, lag( at, 1 ) ), rank( ratio( neg( delta( che, 1 ) ), lag( at, 1 ) ) ) ) ), 1 )

input_signals.name: Peer-Rich Per-Share Sales Decay Issuer
input_signals.hypothesis: Equity issuance by peer-expensive firms should be especially bearish when sales per share had already been deteriorating.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the low-ROA quality overlap with a prior per-share operating-scale diagnostic. Lagging the sales-per-share deterioration reduces mechanical contamination from the current issuance, while the interaction targets firms selling rich equity despite weakening per-share fundamentals.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: winsor( mul( ind_zscore( ratio( mul( prcc_f, csho ), sale ) ), mul( ratio( sstk, lag( at, 1 ) ), rank( neg( lag( growth( ratio( sale, csho ), 1 ), 1 ) ) ) ) ), 1 )
